sources.title: Edward Fadell and Lee Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces
sources.locator: Official eight-page journal scan: §II printed pp. 111–114, Theorems 1–3 and Corollaries 2.1–2.3; §III printed pp. 114–115, Theorems 4–5; opening §IV printed pp. 116–117 through Theorem 6. The scan is image-only; the cited pages were visually inspected.

contents.name: Theorem 1 and its local-coordinate proof, one-point forgetful fiber bundle
Theorem 2, higher homotopy groups from the sequence of fibrations
Corollary 2.1, Euclidean configuration higher homotopy calculation
Corollary 2.2, compact-surface asphericity outside the planar case
contents.reason: The assigned pair concerns the plane and disk. The corollary's general compact-surface statement, including its projective-plane and sphere exceptions, belongs to a separate surface-configuration treatment and is not needed for the planar LES proof.

contents.name: Corollary 2.3, coincidence-free extension of sphere maps
contents.reason: This is an application of higher-homotopy vanishing to extension of sphere maps, not a claim required by the pure-braid, point-pushing or asphericity inventory.

contents.name: Theorem 3, general multi-point forgetting is locally trivial, proof omitted in the original paper
Theorem 4, product triviality for suitable manifolds
contents.reason: The source's suitable-manifold product theorem has stronger hypotheses and a broader manifold scope. This pair constructs only the needed explicit planar section and claims no global product trivialization.

contents.name: Theorem 5, general manifold cross-section criteria and obstructions
contents.reason: The fixed-point and sphere obstruction cases concern manifolds beyond the selected planar page. The explicit far-right planar section is proved separately and avoids those exceptional cases.

contents.name: §IV evaluation-fibration exact sequences for homeomorphism groups
Theorem 6, connectivity bounds for general homeomorphism groups
contents.reason: The general-dimensional connectivity bound exceeds the disk point-pushing comparison and is not used to identify the pure braid forgetful kernel.
